title: Narratives Mislead: An Empirical Study of How LLMs Misjudge CVSS Severity in Bug Bounty Reports
title_zh: 叙事误导：LLM误判漏洞赏金报告CVSS严重性的实证研究

paragraphs.en: 研究构建240份真实赏金报告基准，揭示大模型评估CVSS严重性时系统性高估，最优配置准确率仅约56%。 Bug bounty platforms receive vulnerability reports faster than vendors can triage them, and Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for assigning the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) severity that drives prioritization. Prior evaluations score short CVE descriptions and report accuracy, but deployment depends on how models err, not only how often. CVSS gives each metric a formal meaning that departs from how researchers describe impact in narrative reports, and model rationales suggest that errors concentrate where the two diverge; we ask whether this pattern is systematic. From 4,281 publicly disclosed reports mined from Huntr and HackerOne, we build a benchmark of 240 Huntr reports with vendor-validated CVSS vectors and evaluate eight LLMs under four prompting strategies and fine-tuning, measuring errors by severity class and score and analysing sub-vectors on individual reports. The best prompting configuration reaches only 49.58% level accuracy, ten points above always predicting the majority level, and fine-tuning a 7B model raises this to at most 56.25%, an optimistic upper bound. Errors are directional: models overestimate far more often than they underestimate, and they almost never recognize low-severity vulnerabilities. We trace these errors to three semantic boundaries that the specification draws and narrative reports blur: potential versus realized impact, impact magnitude versus authorization scope, and uncertainty versus the worst case. Because the violations originate partly in the report, we close with an exploratory case study: on four reports, a boundary-aligned, exploit-free report structure lowered a frontier model's score where the narrative invited an unclaimed account takeover, but left the metrics a report does not settle open, and the two published labels disagreed on three of the four reports.
paragraphs.zh: 研究构建240份真实赏金报告基准，揭示大模型评估CVSS严重性时系统性高估，最优配置准确率仅约56%。漏洞赏金平台收到的漏洞报告速度超过了厂商的分诊能力，而大语言模型（LLM）正日益被视为可用于分配驱动优先级排序的通用漏洞评分系统（CVSS）严重性等级。 以往的评估只对简短的CVE描述打分并报告准确率，但能否实际部署取决于模型如何出错，而不仅仅是出错频率。 CVSS为每个指标赋予了正式含义，这与研究者在叙述性报告中描述影响的方式有所不同，且模型的推理依据表明错误集中在两者 diverge 之处；我们要问的是，这一模式是否是系统性的。 我们从Huntr和HackerOne挖掘的4,281份公开披露报告中，构建了一个包含240份Huntr报告的基准，这些报告带有厂商验证的CVSS向量，并在四种提示策略和微调下评估了八个大语言模型，按严重性等级和分数衡量错误，并在单个报告上分析子向量。 最优的提示配置仅达到49.58%的等级准确率，比总是预测多数等级高出十个百分点，而对一个7B模型进行微调最多将其提升到56.25%，这是一个乐观的上限。 错误是有方向性的：模型高估的频率远高于低估，而且它们几乎从不识别低严重性漏洞。 我们将这些错误追溯到规范所划定、而叙述性报告所模糊的三个语义边界：潜在影响与既成影响、影响程度与授权范围、以及不确定性 versus 最坏情形。 由于这些违规部分源自报告本身，我们以一项探索性案例研究作结：在四份报告上，一种与边界对齐、不含漏洞利用描述的报告结构，在叙述性内容暗示可宣称的账户接管情形下降低了前沿模型的评分，但使报告未能确定的指标保持开放，而已发布的两个标签在其中三份报告上并不一致。
